PART I
Item 1. Business
Acme Robotics, Inc. designs, manufactures and services autonomous mobile robots for warehouse fulfilment. Our fleet management software, AcmeOS, coordinates thousands of robots across customer sites and is sold on a subscription basis alongside hardware.
We serve customers in North America and Europe. Our largest customers are third-party logistics providers and grocery retailers. No single customer represented more than 12% of revenue in the fiscal year.
Our strategy is to increase the software share of revenue. Recurring software and services revenue represented 41% of total revenue, compared with 33% in the prior year.
Item 7 of this report discusses the revenue impact of these trends in more detail.
We hold 214 issued patents and 180 pending applications covering navigation, perception and fleet orchestration.
3
Item 1A. Risk Factors
Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below together with the other information in this report.
We operate in a highly competitive market. Competitors range from established industrial automation companies with substantially greater resources to well-funded start-ups. If we fail to compete effectively our revenue and margins would decline.
Our business depends on a limited number of contract manufacturers. Any disruption at these manufacturers, including from natural disasters, labor disputes or financial distress, could delay shipments and harm customer relationships.
Training and operating the machine learning models that power AcmeOS requires significant computing resources. We currently purchase graphics processing capacity from three cloud providers, and increases in the price of that capacity, or constraints on its availability, could materially increase our cost of revenue and delay product improvements.
Changes in trade policy, including the tariffs announced on imported robotic components and lidar sensors, have increased our component costs. We may not be able to pass these costs on to customers, and retaliatory measures could restrict our ability to sell into certain markets.
We are subject to product liability claims. Our robots operate alongside people in customer facilities, and an accident could result in litigation, regulatory action and reputational harm regardless of the outcome of any claim.
We may fail to protect our intellectual property. Despite our patent portfolio, competitors may design around our patents or challenge their validity, and enforcement in some jurisdictions is uncertain.

Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
None.
Item 1C. Cybersecurity
We maintain a cybersecurity risk management program integrated into our enterprise risk management framework. The program is overseen by our Chief Information Security Officer, who reports quarterly to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors.
Our fleet management platform undergoes annual third-party penetration testing. During the fiscal year we did not identify any cybersecurity incidents that materially affected our business strategy, results of operations or financial condition.
We require multi-factor authentication for all employees and contractors, and we conduct phishing simulations at least twice per year.
21
Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
Total revenue for fiscal 2025 was $498.1 million, an increase of 21% compared with the prior year, driven primarily by growth in subscription revenue from AcmeOS and higher robot unit shipments to existing customers.
Gross margin improved as the software share of revenue increased. Operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue as we held headcount approximately flat.
We ended the year with cash and marketable securities sufficient to fund operations for at least the next twelve months. We have no outstanding borrowings under our revolving credit facility.
